main_text.p: ambo currunt : δύο ἀετοὶ ἐπέτονθ, duæ aquilæ volabant.
Sic duobus fingularibus plurale convenit. Xenophon, ἐγὼ καὶ σὺ τὰ δύο χεῖρα τὰς ἀλλήλους ποιήσομεν, ego & tu justa mutuó faciemus.
Dualis rarior eft pro plurali. Homerus,

main_text.p: Latinis anomalia confimilis illa eft, ὁ πολὺς λεὼς χαίρουσι, multitudo popularis gaudent, Lucian. ἐς Ποντον νέμονται ὃ Ταυρικὸν ἔθνος, ad Pontum usq; habitant Taurica gens, Herodot. Sed illud Latinis rarius, ἀχρύετε λεὼς, audite populus, apud Stobæum.
Atticé item neutrum plurale additur fingulari verbo. ut Demofth.

page.notes: Greek passages are printed with heavy accents and partly faint; several Greek words are uncertain and may contain errors. The Greek lines at "ἰσε γὰρ" and "ἐς Ποντον" are particularly doubtful. The mark "x" at the foot is taken as a signature. A few words in the scan are obscured by stains.
